title: Elevated KIF2C Expression Drives Osteosarcoma Progression by Modulating the Wnt/beta-Catenin Signaling Pathway and Contributing to an Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment.
authors: Liu, Ya-Yun; Sun, Wu; Liu, Lin; Cheng, Jin-Hui; Li, Jing-Tang; Huang, Zu-Tai; Ouyang, Min
one_liner_zh: 该文研究KIF2C在骨肉瘤中通过Wnt/β-catenin通路促进肿瘤进展及免疫抑制微环境，虽含分子对接与动力学，但核心非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although kinesin family member 2C (KIF2C) is implicated in various cancers, its role in osteosarcoma (OS) and the associated inflammatory microenvironment remains unclear. METHODS: Publicly available datasets were analyzed to determine KIF2C expression, diagnostic value, and prognostic relevance in OS. In vitro (proliferation, colony formation, apoptosis, migration, invasion) and in vivo assays assessed its biological functions. KEGG enrichment and GSVA explored underlying pathways. ssGSEA, ESTIMATE algorithms, and single-cell sequencing evaluated the immune context, and molecular docking and molecular dynamics identified potential inhibitory compounds. RESULTS: KIF2C was significantly overexpressed in OS, effectively distinguishing OS from normal tissues. Elevated KIF2C levels correlated with poor survival outcomes. Silencing KIF2C suppressed OS cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and in vivo tumor growth, while promoting apoptosis; conversely, overexpression of KIF2C had the opposite effect. Mechanistically, co-immunoprecipitation results indicated that KIF2C can bind to beta-catenin to regulate the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway. Furthermore, high KIF2C expression was associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment characterized by immune exhaustion. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics suggested butein as a candidate small-molecule inhibitor targeting KIF2C-related oncogenic mechanisms. CONCLUSION: KIF2C drives OS progression by enhancing Wnt/beta-catenin signaling and fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Targeting KIF2C may offer new therapeutic approaches in managing OS.
abstract_zh: 背景：尽管驱动蛋白家族成员2C（KIF2C）与多种癌症相关，但其在骨肉瘤（OS）中的作用及相关的炎症微环境仍不清楚。方法：分析公开可用的数据集，以确定KIF2C在OS中的表达、诊断价值及预后相关性。通过体外实验（增殖、集落形成、凋亡、迁移、侵袭）和体内实验评估其生物学功能。利用KEGG富集和GSVA探索潜在通路。采用ssGSEA、ESTIMATE算法和单细胞测序评估免疫环境，并通过分子对接和分子动力学识别潜在抑制化合物。结果：KIF2C在OS中显著过表达，能有效区分OS与正常组织。KIF2C水平升高与较差的生存结果相关。沉默KIF2C抑制了OS细胞增殖、迁移、侵袭及体内肿瘤生长，同时促进凋亡；相反，KIF2C过表达则产生相反效果。机制上，免疫共沉淀结果表明KIF2C可与β-catenin结合，调节Wnt/β-catenin通路。此外，KIF2C高表达与以免疫耗竭为特征的免疫抑制肿瘤微环境相关。分子对接和分子动力学提示butein是靶向KIF2C相关致癌机制的候选小分子抑制剂。结论：KIF2C通过增强Wnt/β-catenin信号传导并促进免疫抑制微环境，驱动OS进展。靶向KIF2C可能为OS治疗提供新途径。
